name: Clojure
typeSystem: Dynamic, strong; runs on the JVM (or JavaScript via ClojureScript) and emphasises immutable, persistent data structures (vectors, maps, sets) shared efficiently through structural sharing rather than in-place mutation.
runtime: Compiles to JVM bytecode at load time (or ahead-of-time), then benefits from the standard JVM JIT; ClojureScript instead compiles to JavaScript.

runtimes.name: JVM (HotSpot)
runtimes.role: Primary target: Clojure forms compile to JVM bytecode, then JIT-compile like any other JVM bytecode.

runtimes.name: ClojureScript (compiles to JS)
runtimes.role: Compiles Clojure syntax to JavaScript for browsers and Node.js.

runtimes.name: babashka (SCI in a GraalVM native image)
runtimes.role: Fast-starting scripting environment whose native executable interprets a substantial subset of Clojure through SCI.

compilers.name: clojure (JVM compiler)
compilers.role: Compiles Clojure forms to JVM bytecode, typically on the fly as code loads.

concurrencyModel: Software transactional memory (refs) for coordinated synchronous state, atoms for uncoordinated synchronous state, agents for asynchronous state, and core.async for CSP-style channels and lightweight processes.

codeExample.caption: Hello, World! plus a recursive factorial
